notes.title: Caffeine Update - Sorry Everyone
notes.content:
Hey all, 
I am so sorry for not updating sooner, and for not being on top of things recently.
I realize i owe all of you much more than I have offered so far, the main reason for the slow pace of everything is a combination of full-time work & now having a family. 
I gravely underestimated the amount of time that these things would take up and how it would affect my work on Caffeine.
So for now I am not talking about dates or episode two, I am going to be taking it one step at a time and the first part of that will be to finish the update i promised to episode one and then finish work on episode two.

Again i'm sorry for all this but i hope i can redeem myself somehow by getting these updates & episodes out.

thank you for your patience and thank you to those of you who have poked me on twitter to encourage me to keep going.

Dylan

notes.title: Caffeine - Episode One Update Plan
notes.content:
Hello there, 
As promised I am here writing this out tonight!

While there are a few people that do like the game so far, I can see there are some problems with Episode One in it's current state a few things also did not turn out exactly as good as they could have in the game. I have been working hard behind the scenes slowly re-writing a heap of the games underlying systems and plan to flesh out areas which seem to have been neglected in the caffeine ridden world in the coming months with multiple updates to the game.

I will be posting once a week here about the progress and any upcoming content to be added to the game.

While there isn't a huge amount to show yet (most of it so far has been behind the scenes) I can reveal that so far these re-writes along with a newer engine version have boosted Caffeine's frame-rate by almost double which i think is great news!

I will be pushing this optimization out in the next couple of weeks and will be sure to make a fuss once it goes live.

Anyway thanks for your support and patience towards a lowly part time one man dev :)

Cheers
Dylan

notes.title: Caffeine - Episode One - Update v112 for Mac
notes.content:
The v112 update for Caffeine - Episode One has been released today for the Mac platform. 

This patch brings the Mac version in line with Windows and Linux versions.

Thanks to everyone who has been working with me by sending in bug reports and suggestions, your help has been invaluable. 

Update v112 For Mac

Notes
If you experience low performance give disabled shadows a try, with this patch it still looks great but will give up to a 50% fps increase. 
If you are still getting any crashes please email support@incandescentimaging.net 

Fixed

Major issue where the player could not move at all on launch.
Optimized shadow casting lights 
Fixed sun light leaking when shadows were disabled (Game now looks great even without shadows!) 
Updated to 4.9.2 engine base 
Fixed some objects being culled before they were off screen 
Fixed all known physics bugs 
Fixed the player being thrown out of the elevator into space 
Fixed shadow settings being reset when getting a checkpoint 
Default settings on first run are now much better optimized with a 50% performance increase compared to the original defaults. 
Optimized the number of shadow casting lights for a slight performance increase. 
Added / Tweaked subtle bounce lighting to all toggle lights in the game. 
Various performance tweaks. 

Added

Opened up two rooms on level seven 
Airlock on level five 
Torch that does not break after 15 seconds

notes.title: Caffeine - Episode One - v105 Patch
notes.content:
Performance Fix #1

Good evening all, 
I just pushed a small patch which added the ability to turn off the in game sun in the settings menu, as well as disabling the sun when shadows are turned off so that the game still looks great with shadows disabled. 

Disabling shadows usually provides up to a 50% performance increase at the moment so having the game still look good with them disabled is very important.

Stay tuned for a larger update tomorrow evening.
Thanks for being patient and enjoy your night!
Cheers
Dylan

notes.title: Caffeine - Episode One - v104 Patch
notes.content:
Today a patch has been released to address most of the launch bugs / day one issues.

This is just the start of many updates to come to improve both the game experience and to fix current issues players are having with the game.

Added

- Small tutorial system in the first area, familiarizes player with gameplay concepts.

-Renamed the Steam store package to Caffeine - Season One to avoid confusion as to what you are buying.

Fixed

- Texture streaming (All notes and terminals are now readable on any graphical setting)

- Various collision glitches (No more loosing the first keycard inside the monitor)

- Game now remembers graphics options and applies them at startup.

- The two checkpoint saves in the game are now working.

- Physics (Objects are now much less likely to break the space time continuum)

- Small performance increase from complete obliteration of static lighting.

- BSOD after 10 mins of playing.

notes.title: Linux Release & Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

So we had a bit of a rocky release, I believe I can still turn it around.

Most Issues Now Fixed

First off the bat I would like to note that I have been trying to keep up with all the bug reports and will be sending out a patch today to mainly address the note textures not rendering properly in some situations.

That being said I have patched out pretty much all of the bugs described in the first two negative reviews on Steam, so they should all be fixed as that patch went up on day one.

All of you please know that I have been reading almost everything that is being posed here and I am vowing to get everything fixed and make Episode One better, before moving over completely to Episode Two development.

Linux Support Is Here

I am glad to announce that the Linux version of Caffeine is now up and running on Steam!

notes.title: Caffeine Pre-Release Demo Update - 7/11/14
notes.content:
After a good few days with my brand new Oculus Rift DK2, I have prepared a patch for the Caffeine Demo on Steam.

Non-Oculus Features

Implementation of Distance Field Ray-traced Shadows - Awesome penumbra, no shadow-map aliasing and better performance!
Large performance boost - R9 280 hits up to 80fps on max settings at 1080p (Level streaming still causing some jarring hiccups).
Menu system is in development - Very basic at the moment (does not render correctly in Oculus at this time).

Oculus Features

Hotkey to switch between Oculus appropriate settings - Dynamic shadows are currently disabled for Rift settings as the DFRT Shadows have some strange issues in stereo at this time.
Hotkey to reset orientation / head position.

Another patch will be released sometime in the next month with more performance and the inclusion of a shadow method that will work well in VR.

notes.title: Caffeine Development Update - October 2014
notes.content:
Welcome to the October Development Update for Caffeine!

The State Of Caffeine

The core components of Caffeine are coming along quite nicely, below are a few tidbits of what I have been working on in the past month!

 Optimizations

When the demo for Caffeine was released on Steam last month, it's performance was below average and was only hitting about 30fps on a R9 280 at 1080p. Because of this I have been working on getting this figure way up to not only provide a good experience on PC but also to prepare for the lower spec of certain consoles and the 75fps target of the Oculus Rift.

So far the results have been great, and I feel I am almost reaching where i want to be in terms of base performance to move ahead with more level design.

Some screenshots with relevant FPS captured on a R9 280 coupled with an AMD FX-8120.

View Screenshots

Please note: These screenshots were taken without SSR(Screen Space Reflections) as I was testing for potential Oculus performance, they cost me up to 10fps depending on the area.
Once I have the optimizations completed I will merge them back into the demo build for you all to check out!

 

Other News

Oculus Rift DK2

It looks like Caffeine's DK2 will be arriving whenever Oculus decide that Australia deserves another batch, so let's hope that's soon!

GCAP 2014 & Pax Australia

I managed to get selected to benefit from the GCAP Assist program which means that I will be at GCAP 14 in 10 days time (28th Oct) and I will also be staying in Melbourne for Pax Australia later that week!

Be sure to say hi of you attend and happen to spot me!

 

Have a safe weekend,

Dylan
